chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban told us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Ruba'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then, let them end their tafath". He said: The cutting of the moustache and nails.

key_terms.تَفَث: Ritual grooming or trimming, specifically referring to cutting nails and moustaches

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'tafath' refer to in the context of Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) provides a concise exegetical definition of 'tafath' as the physical grooming of trimming the mustache and cutting nails. This interpretation highlights the practical aspect of *fitrah* (natural disposition) within the ritual purification (*taharah*) required during Hajj or Umrah, linking bodily cleanliness directly to spiritual compliance. The chain of transmission underscores the reliability of this understanding within the early Shia scholarly tradition.
